bastinado: beating the soles of the feet with a stick as punishment
ssegai: a short spear with a narrow iron blade, thrown or thrust
targe: a small round shield carried for protection in fighting
uezzin: the crier who calls Muslims to prayer from the mosque
haykh: an Arab tribal chief or elder with authority over others
rosary: a string of beads used by Catholics to count prayers
coralline: resembling coral in form, colour, or texture
gaudy: showy and brightly coloured, but cheap or tasteless
draughts: the board game played with round pieces, called checkers in America
chaunt: an old spelling of chant; a sung or intoned religious recitation
deleterious: harmful or damaging to health or well-being
quiver: a case for carrying arrows, usually worn on the back
auditors: listeners or hearers of a speech, sermon, or performance
couch: a long low piece of furniture for lying or reclining on
scant: barely enough; small in amount or hardly sufficient
egress: a way out or the act of leaving a place
thence: from that place or from that time, then
whence: from what place or source, from where
destitute: lacking the basic necessities of life, such as food or shelter
ignoble: not noble in character, mean or dishonourable
rapacity: greedy eagerness to seize wealth or goods by force
chieftainship: the position, rank, or authority of a tribal chief
propitiated: appeased or soothed the anger of a god or person
prodigious: enormous in size, amount, or degree; remarkable
craft: a boat, ship, or other vessel used for travel on water
seaboard: the coastline or shore of a country or region
ominous: suggesting that something bad is about to happen
flitted: moved lightly and quickly from place to place
muffled: deadened or softened so that sound is hard to hear
barbarous: cruel, uncivilised, or lacking refinement and education
savage: uncivilised or fierce; a person regarded as primitive by Europeans
fetisism: worship of objects believed to hold magical or spiritual power
witch: a person believed to practise magic, often with evil intent
kettledrum: a large copper drum with a skin head, tuned by tightening
congregation: the assembled group of worshippers at a religious service
pulpit: a raised platform in a church from which a preacher speaks
sheet: a large piece of cloth, here used as a wrap or covering
grease: animal fat, often used for cooking or as an ointment
fellow: a man, often a companion or a person of the same group
dervish: a member of a Muslim religious order known for ascetic devotion
superintendent: an official in charge of a department, station, or establishment
preacher: a person who delivers religious sermons to a congregation
discourse: a formal speech or lengthy discussion on a subject
mercy: compassion shown to someone who could be punished or harmed
caravan: a group of travellers or merchants journeying together, often with animals
contempt: a feeling that someone is worthless or beneath respect
prelude: an introductory event or piece that comes before the main part
neglect: failure to give proper care, attention, or respect to something
